_notes: B11 — Crew-out to individual time-outs (catalog B11, plan test-plans/journey-b/b11-crew-out.md, recording docs/media/journey-b/b11-crew-out.mp4, PET-12649 automation / WEBPET-1530 manual, runner row B11-001). Transport, not simulation, happy path only.

One crew-out fans out, device-side, into one TimeOut record per still-active crew member — the importer never mints a CO reference itself, so the envelope supplies it explicitly, exactly as B1's CI does. A time-out row (crew-out or individual) carries no Job, Ranch or Field: the device's LookupContents for it is Employee:Code|Crew:Code only (expected.envelope.absentInSection). The early leaver 6003 already timed out individually (TO, BarcodeBadge, 15:09) before the crew-out (CO, Crew, 15:10) and stays untouched by it.

Six records: the 07:15 crew-in for 6001/6002/6003 (CI, Crew, full work context), 6003's individual time-out, then the crew-out fanned out into two rows for 6001 and 6002 at the same instant — the three time-outs share one GPS fix. dayOffset -4 is B11's own fixture day (workers=2 duplicate-Time-In guard). No header punchTime — the old envelope passed none.

cardType null: the envelope mixes cardType 1 (crew-in) and 0 (time-out), so the office read queries every type. absentEmployees: 6004 never appears. verification cards: no Transfer grid — the office UI this exercises is the relay pull, and the one datum unique to View ▸ Time Cards (Employee Selection) is asserted on the API as employeeSource.

expected.cards[].employeeSourceCode is the raw EmployeeSource enum the API returns — 13 = Crew (the crew-out rows), 2 = BarcodeBadge (the individual time-out). It is on the response but not on the named OfficeTimeCard fields, so the spec reads it through the index signature. Residual risk (Planner-flagged): value 2 has no live precedent on dev — report, don't delete, if only that assert fails.
cleanup: the timeCards step sweeps the four crew members' fixture day before the import and deletes the imported cards after the test; the flow passes sweep:false so exactly one cleanup path is live.
